name: Pramod Mahajan
role: Indian BJP strategist and union minister for telecommunications, information technology and parliamentary affairs
summary: Mahajan promoted global economic integration and private telecom competition while retaining a public-service role for government. He backed the Ram temple campaign, a uniform civil code and removal of Kashmir’s special autonomy.

public-ownership.rationale: Promotes private telecom competition but retains and strengthens public firms; ownership policy is mixed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Criticises excessive IT regulation while defending statutory telecom regulation; the preferred degree is mixed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Defends warrantless cybercrime searches by senior police officers while requiring technical training.

more-religion-public.rationale: Affirms his commitment to the Ram temple campaign as a political cause.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Promotes reconstruction of a grand Ram temple at Ayodhya as an important public objective.

free-trade.rationale: Urges compulsory global economic integration rather than inward-looking industrial comparisons.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Demands public investment in power and transport infrastructure.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Maintains publicly supported universal rural telecom provision beyond basic security functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rejects second-class treatment of non-Hindus and says governing Muslims requires winning their trust.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Reaffirms in his final Thapar interview that a uniform civil code should apply nationally.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Describes resisting Indira Gandhi’s Emergency as a struggle for freedom.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Calls for a disciplined party governed by collective decisions in his final interview.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Explains the pornography offence while distinguishing offenders from unaware internet service providers.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Wants common civil law rather than separate religious personal-law systems.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Maintains the party will obey the Supreme Court’s Ayodhya decision despite its temple preference.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Explicitly urges good people to enter politics to improve the country.

native-born-offices.rationale: Declares a foreign-origin prime minister unacceptable, specifically objecting to Sonia Gandhi.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Calls the removed Babri structure an eyesore and supports replacing it with a grand temple.

non-intervention.rationale: Supports international action against terrorism extending beyond bin Laden and Afghanistan.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Uses asserted prior temple occupation to reject rebuilding a mosque at the disputed site.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Opposes Emergency repression and defends political opponents’ freedom to criticise his leadership.

abolish-ip.rationale: Explicitly retains copyright remedies and proposes adapting copyright enforcement to digital offences.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Supports India becoming a nuclear-armed state rather than excluding nuclear weapons.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Advocates withdrawing Kashmir’s special constitutional powers through parliamentary amendment.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Supports developing the nuclear option and presents India’s tests as meeting national security needs.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Explicitly reaffirms removal of Jammu and Kashmir’s Article 370 autonomy in 2006.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Praises lower telecom sales taxes and reduced customs duties on mobile phones.

notes: Whole-career review includes Emergency opposition, parliamentary politics, telecom and IT legislation, the temple movement, nuclear policy and interviews through 2006. His 2004 language about moderation on Article 370 is superseded by explicit opposition in the 2006 Thapar interview, reproduced in the collected statements. The same collection reproduces a TIME interview and a Neena Vyas interview; their original questions are distinguished from his answers. The 2006 infrastructure speech is used narrowly. State support for public telecom firms coexists with private entry; licensing favouritism allegations are disputed and are not treated as established corruption or general approval of business privileges. The temple position does not establish support for scriptural law or racial citizenship. Counterterrorism cooperation does not establish approval of every subsequent war. Family allegations and his murder provide no evidence of positions on criminal punishment or gender rights. All remaining null statements reviewed across ten themes; no positions inferred from BJP or RSS affiliation.
